editorial.headline: Contract Packaging, Open Nationally and in Bali
editorial.standfirst: A broad contracted packaging activity, open across all stated enterprise scales and available for full foreign ownership nationally and PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
Other Packaging Activities is a contracted packaging service with a deliberately broad practical reach. It covers bottling liquids, packing solid objects, labelling, marking and sterilising products when those tasks are carried out for a fee or under contract. It also includes the packing of parcels or gifts and the wrapping of gifts. The work may be delivered through an automated process or manually. In other words, the defined activity is the packaging work performed as a service: preparing an item, identifying it where needed, and completing the packaging treatment specified in the record. It is not confined to a single packaging technology or type of item.

Who can register is equally clear. The activity is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar enterprises. This is a full stated scale range, rather than a scope limited to a single business class or a single production method. A small operator using manual handling and a larger organisation using automation are both contemplated by the activity’s language, provided the work remains within the listed packaging, labelling, marking, sterilisation, parcel-packing or gift-wrapping services. The scale labels set the available registration range; the scope sets the kind of work.

Nationally, the PMA status is TERBUKA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. That permits full foreign ownership at the national level for this activity. The point is straightforward but important: the national PMA position follows the stated status and ceiling, while the operational description explains the services that form the activity. The source recorded for that PMA position is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. Nothing in the scope narrows the service to only automated work, only manual work, only liquids or only gifts; each format is expressly within its described reach.

Bali does not reverse the national position. The provincial record says that, at the Besar scale, the OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi; it therefore records the activity as not blocked by Bali’s moratorium. That moratorium is island-wide and permanent for PMA activities with low or medium-low risk. This activity is recorded outside that block, so a foreign investor can register it in Bali today. The distinction remains important: 100% is the national foreign-ownership ceiling, while Bali’s recorded conclusion concerns registration under its risk-based moratorium.
editorial.pullQuote: Bali does not reverse the national position.
